summary: T11 delivered and verified the gost-relay/ssh/ssr subset. mieru, masque and sudoku were investigated against the locked v1.19.34 tree and the local module/crate caches; the concrete blockers and executable next steps are recorded here. They are not claimed as implemented. T13 later delivered mieru (clean-room TCP) and removed its GPL-derived sudoku port (T13-A3; clean-room rewrite is T17).

completed.gost-relay: TCP/TLS/auth/forward; controlled Rust peer + CLI success tunnel; option matrix rows
completed.ssh: password/inline PEM/host-key/direct-tcpip; controlled russh peer + CLI success tunnel; MSRV raised to 1.89
completed.ssr: all pinned stream ciphers + origin/plain; independent Go server + Go cipher vectors + CLI success tunnel

source.protocol_source: pkg/protocol (34 Go files, 10,717 lines including tests): session.go 1511, underlay_stream.go 910, mux.go 881, underlay_packet.go 859, metadata.go 362, segment.go 368, low_entropy.go 242, padding.go 214; pkg/cipher 1,843 lines

mieru.license: GPL-3.0 (module LICENSE); Billow native-kernel is MIT
blockers: No Rust port or wire-compatible crate exists in the tree; the protocol needs PBKDF2-SHA256 time-salt keys, XChaCha20-Poly1305 with nonce patching, 32-byte metadata, segment padding, optional low-entropy modes, session open/data/ack/close, flow-control windows and optional mux/handshake modes.

Vendoring the GPL-3.0 Go module into the MIT Rust crate is a licensing conflict. A Go test server can be built from the locked module as a separate process, but the client must be a clean-room implementation from docs/protocol.md plus Go vectors.
No controlled mieru server has been built in this attempt; the module is available locally but no config/peer harness exists yet.
next_steps: T13 decision: clean-room TCP single-session client first (PBKDF2-SHA256, XChaCha20-Poly1305, session open/data/close, no mux/low-entropy), with Go-generated segment vectors; then UDP associate and mux.

Build the controlled server from the local module (e.g. `go run ./cmd/mita` with a generated config) as a separate GPL test fixture; record the build command and keep it out of the shipped Rust binary.
If the license/effort decision is to defer, keep the current explicit `[unsupported]` rejection and remove it from T11 compatibility claims.
mieru.outcome: T13 delivered the clean-room TCP single-session client; the blockers above refer to the GPL module and were resolved by implementing from docs/protocol.md (peer evidence in protocol-peers.json#t13).

source.imports: github.com/metacubex/http, transport/masque, transport/tuic/common; HTTP/3 CONNECT-IP/CONNECT-UDP plus an IP stack

local_dependencies.missing: h3, h3-quinn, an IP stack crate; crates.io/network was unavailable during this attempt
local_dependencies.note: T10 has not pinned the shared QUIC dependency profile yet; T7 owns the 40 MB memory measurement.

blockers: HTTP/3 CONNECT-IP/CONNECT-UDP needs an h3 stack and an IP stack; only quinn is cached, so the dependency set cannot be built offline.
The QUIC/IP-stack memory profile must align with T10 and be measured by T7 before adoption; adding it silently would violate the shared dependency decision.
next_steps: T14 (after T10 pins quinn/h3 versions): add h3 + h3-quinn + the chosen IP stack, implement CONNECT-UDP (RFC 9298) and CONNECT-IP (RFC 9484) with capsules, verify against a controlled HTTP/3 peer built from the locked quic-go tree or a Rust h3 server, and record RSS for T7.
If the dependency decision is not ready, keep the explicit rejection and do not claim masque compatibility.

source.key_files: handshake.go 537, early_handshake.go 340, kip.go 257, multiplex.go/multiplex_dialer.go, httpmask tunnel, crypto/, obfs/, tables.go/table_probe.go, uot.go

blockers: 13,577 lines of custom handshake/KIP/table-driven crypto/HTTP-mask/multiplexing; no Rust port or crate exists.
A partial port would not be wire-compatible; the handshake, table layout and KIP message framing are all required before any tunnel can be verified.
No controlled sudoku server harness exists in this attempt; the locked tree contains both sides but building and driving them is a separate task.
next_steps: T13 split: (a) build a controlled server from the locked transport/sudoku and capture handshake/KIP vectors, (b) port the handshake + KIP + table layout for a single TCP session, (c) add HTTP mask and multiplexing, (d) verify success/auth-failure/boundary cases.
If the split is not approved, keep the explicit rejection and record sudoku as deferred rather than partially compatible.
sudoku.outcome: T13-A3 (2026-11-22): the first T13 port was translated from the GPL-3.0 `transport/sudoku` and was removed; `type: sudoku` is rejected by name again. Any implementation of the steps above must be clean-room (wire observations and the public protocol shape only, never the pinned Go source); the task is T17. Audit: evidence/t13-a3-sudoku-removal.md
